messages:
alex_cust: Hi team, since last night our requests to api.redwood.ai are sporadically hitting eu endpoints and we get 403s. Our service is hosted in us-west and this started after a proxy update.

maya_support: Hey Alex — can you confirm deployment type (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC) and paste a redacted curl or example response headers?

alex_cust: Private VPC. Minimal repro:

```
curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/meta
```

We added some proxy headers for tracing: `X-SNAT-Pool: pool-3a` and `X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.22`. Our egress infra uses a small pool of public SNAT IPs and the controller started cycling pools between regions.

ravi_sre: That cycling would explain Smart Router choosing different regions. Do you have a tcpdump or netstat showing the SYN source IP and the public SNAT mapping? Even one line is enough.

alex_cust: tcpdump extract (redacted):
```
14:11:02.001 IP 10.10.2.5.50020 > 52.14.200.19.443: Flags [S], seq 321
14:11:02.023 IP 198.51.100.22 > 52.14.200.19.443: Flags [S], seq 654
```
The public 198.51.100.22 resolves to an ISP range that geo-locates to EU.

eva_neteng: Confirmed pattern — public SNAT geolocation is being used as a tie-breaker in our routing decision for private deployments where no explicit hint is present. Two quick questions: (1) does your proxy rotate SNAT IPs across different physical egress pools? (2) can you set a stable header we can trust instead of X-Forwarded-For which is frequently rewritten?

alex_cust: The proxy controller does rotate because we autoscale egress nodes. We can emit a stable label header, e.g. `X-Org-Egress-Pool: us-west-01`. Would that be useful?

maya_support: Yes — we can whitelist a mutually agreed header. Also short-term you can send an explicit region hint header we support internally: `X-RWD-Region-Hint: us-west-2`. That forces the router to prefer US region for the request.

ravi_sre: I'll open an infra config ticket to add a routing exception for your account while you stabilize egress. Long term, recommended fixes: use a US-only SNAT pool or advertise a stable egress pool label that maps to US IPs.

alex_cust: Is `X-RWD-Region-Hint` documented? We couldn't find it publicly.

eva_neteng: It's an internal compatibility header for private setups — we don't publish it widely. If you want to avoid header-based hacks later, we can work with you to reserve a contiguous US SNAT range.

maya_support: Can you run this command and paste the response headers only?

```
curl -i -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"X-RWD-Trace: debug-xyz\" \
  -H \"X-Org-Egress-Pool: us-west-01\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/meta
```

alex_cust: Without the `X-RWD-Region-Hint` we get: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
x-rwd-error: auth_region_mismatch
x-redwood-region: eu-west-1
```
With `X-RWD-Region-Hint: us-west-2` we see: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-redwood-region: us-west-2
x-request-id: rwd-xyz789
```

ravi_sre: Ok that's consistent. I'm creating INFRA-TICKET-4599 to add a temporary override so your account will prefer us-west even if SNAT geolocates to EU. We'll also add monitoring to alert if your egress IPs change geo.

infra-bot: INFRA-TICKET-4599 created. Change request queued for canary rollout to account alex-company. Approver: @ravi_sre.

ravi_sre: Approving canary, rolling out override to 5% of traffic then 100% if green. Alex, can you run a few calls after I flip it and report latency + status?

alex_cust: Will do, testing in 5m. Thanks.

(5 minutes later)

alex_cust: Update: after the override is in place requests are consistently landing in us-west and 403s stopped. Latency ~40ms. Rolling rotation of SNAT pool still on, but override prevents wrong-region auth failures.

eva_neteng: Great. Next step if you want: schedule a short call so we can design a static US SNAT pool or reserve an egress appliance in us-west to avoid relying on header hints.

maya_support: Leaving this thread open while Alex confirms follow-up plan. If you prefer, we can attach a network migration playbook to the ticket.

alex_cust: We'll go for static SNAT pool. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ravi_sre: Closing loop on this thread. Ticket INFRA-TICKET-4599 will include rollback plan and an automated check that asserts `x-redwood-region` == `us-west-2` for a sample request.

maya_support: Marking thread resolved in Slack, keeping the infra ticket open for follow-up.
